content: Discussion thread for #General announcements > CSLib Initiative

I'll ask some questions publicly since politely asking in private seems to have elicited no change in the level of communication. It seems extremely unclear if there's any coordination between this CSLib Initiative and the existing reviewers and maintainers. I still have no idea about:

  • If there will be any sort of coordination between maintainers/reviewers
  • Anything concrete about the aims of the Initiative and how it aligns with ongoing work
  • Decisions about hiring (were there job public listings?) or how priorities were determined here.

Quite frankly, the answer seems to be a resounding "no" to the question of coordination, since I was I believe the first area maintainer added to the project and am completely in the dark here. It makes me seriously reconsider if this project is a good place to continue the same level of effort that I've been providing in code review, contributions and maintaining Mathlib compatibility.

I mean no disrespect to @Jesse Alama though. I have personally found his contributions valuable and am glad to see this recognized! (I am unfamiliar with @Guilherme Lima's work that has not yet appeared in CSLib, but wish you the best as well!)

Some relevant links I found:
https://www.cslib.io/initiative/ (added on Aug 5)
https://www.renaissancephilanthropy.org/insights/cslib-initiative-qanda

I'm surprised none of these things were mentioned on Zulip before. It sounds exciting, but I hope the communication with all the CSLib maintainers can be improved!

Thank you, @Floris van Doorn , for sharing the links. We broadly announced the Initiative on LinkedIn and X, and we got many reactions from the community members on these channels. But we forgot to share the links here in Zulip! As always, we sometimes forget the obvious.

As https://www.cslib.io/strategic-organizations/ says, the Initiative is one of CSLib's Strategic Organizations. It aims to support its adoption and growth.

Regarding communication with the maintainers, we are working to clarify things through the proper channel. I hope Chris's post above doesn't suggest we ignored him. On the contrary, we have DMs with him, but we were surprised by this post, which reveals that we left questions unanswered.

X is increasingly a poor place for any kind of announcement or discussion meant for a public audience, rather than the self-selected community who have chosen to create or keep accounts there over the past four years. For example, many people here prefer to post links to XCancel so discussions are properly accessible to people without accounts on X, but XCancel was shut down for two weeks recently because of legal threats from X.

Following on from @Joseph Myers comment. More generally, I wish for things like this the community was involved right from the outset. There have been numerous occasions over the years within the Lean community where things have been done behind closed doors which have a large impact on the community - and when announced had people (IMO rightly) put-off. To me projects like CSLib, Mathlib and Physlib are community projects, and decisions about them should be made at the community level. I know this is unavoidable in some cases, but I think it is the thing we should strive for.
